- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if spike occurs.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model shows strong upward bias, cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00), especially in 30d horizon — apply lag correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–5 days after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility — use 14-day smoothed average as baseline, then adjust ±2% based on sentiment direction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 values, model often fails to correct for overbought conditions — apply downward bias of 3–5% in next 5–7 days unless confirmed by new data.
